newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish ammunition factory blasts kill one.
newsitem.headline: Turkish ammunition factory blasts kill one.

text.p: A series of explosions at an ammunition factory in central Turkey shook the town of Kirikkale on Thursday, killing one person, injuring dozens and spreading panic.

A huge blast shortly after 3.30 p.m. killed one man and damaged a helicopter being used to fight a blaze at the plant, state-run Anatolian news agency reported. It said the man had been struck by a piece of shrapnel.
Witnesses said the explosion sent glass and debris flying and broke windows across a large area.

Anatolian said dozens people, including police and soldiers, had been cut by flying debris and were being treated in makeshift field clinics. The town's hospital was evacuated because of concerns about further explosions.
The southern district of Kirikkale was evacuated after the first blast at 8.50 a.m., which was followed by intermittent explosions.

"We were woken up by the explosion," Ramazan Karacabay, a retired factory worker, told Reuters. "All of us ran away from our houses. Lots of windows were broken. We were frightened and left the area."
A fire in the factory continued to burn and thick smoke billowed above the area, where earlier streets were crowded with traffic as people left for other parts of the town.
Firefighting helicopters doused the area with water, but their work was suspended after the latest explosion.
Turkey's interior, defence and industry ministers held a crisis committee meeting with the regional governor to consider on a course of action, Anatolian said.
The interior minister estimated the damage to be at least one trillion Turkish lira ($6.7 million).
Six factory workers were injured, one seriously, in the original blast. The cause was unclear.
"There is no probability of sabotage," Kirikkale mayor Cemalettin Akdogan was quoted by Anatolian as saying.
A fireman speaking by phone from Kirikkale fire station told Reuters:
"There are enough explosives in this factory to blow up the whole town. It is not possible to approach the factory."
State oil refiner Tupras has a refinery in the area, but it was far enough away not to be affected by the explosions, a Tupras official told Reuters.
But he said filling activities had been halted temporarily as a precaution.
